title: The Final Inheritance
premise: When the coffin of town founder Aldous Vane is exhumed for a bicentennial ceremony and found empty, cathedral archivist Kestrel Galloway is drawn into a mystery that reaches back two hundred years. Following clues hidden in the cathedral's donation ledger — a cipher of marginalia and misfiled dates — she discovers that Vane faked his own death to escape justice for a massacre he ordered, and that a secret society of descendants has been paying an 'inheritance' ever since to keep the truth buried. The trail leads to a living heir who has been using the crypt as a prison, and Kestrel must choose between exposing the crime and protecting the innocent descendant held captive below. In the end she opens the crypt publicly, delivers the ledger to the town, and accepts that justice outside the law costs her her post — but frees the town from its founding lie.
about_author: O. M. Eriksen is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing church archives in coastal New England before turning to fiction. They write mysteries rooted in old documents, small-town complicity, and the quiet violence of respectable institutions.

chapters.title: The Weight of Dust
chapters.summary: Kestrel Galloway catalogs the cathedral's restricted archive, establishing her pride in closed cases and her uneasy relationship with the locked crypt door. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: controlled order about to be shattered.

chapters.title: An Empty Coffin
chapters.summary: The bicentennial exhumation of founder Aldous Vane reveals nothing but lead weights and a scrap of 1820s newspaper. The mayor panics; the bishop blames vandalism. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: shock beneath professional composure.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Lies
chapters.summary: Kestrel notices impossible entries in the original donation ledger — payments dated after Vane's death. She begins copying them secretly. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt awakening.

chapters.title: The Founder's Circle
chapters.summary: Kestrel interviews the Vane Historical Society, whose members close ranks with practiced smiles. One elderly member, Ruth Ambrose, slips her a warning. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: first sense of institutional menace.

chapters.title: Cipher in the Margins
chapters.summary: Working nights, Kestrel decodes the ledger's marginalia into a sequence of names and dates — a payment schedule spanning two centuries. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: dread mixed with exhilaration.

chapters.title: What Ruth Remembered
chapters.summary: Ruth Ambrose recounts her childhood glimpse of a figure entering the crypt on the anniversary of Vane's burial. That night someone ransacks Kestrel's office. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: fear arriving at her doorstep.

chapters.title: The Massacre at Harrow Fen
chapters.summary: Archive research uncovers the suppressed story: eleven tenant families evicted and burned out on land Vane wanted, officially blamed on 'fever.' POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: moral vertigo — the beloved founder was a monster.

chapters.title: A Death That Never Was
chapters.summary: Kestrel reconstructs how Vane staged his death, fled abroad, and returned in disguise; the crypt's inner chamber was built for him to live — or be kept. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: grim clarity.

chapters.title: The Inheritance
chapters.summary: The decoded ledger resolves into its purpose: an annual 'inheritance' paid by Vane's heirs to a keeper of the crypt. Someone still collects it. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: the past is not past.

chapters.title: Threats in Good Taste
chapters.summary: The mayor offers Kestrel a promotion and a transfer; the bishop hints at her precarious employment. Both smiles hide threats. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: pressure to look away.

chapters.title: Ruth's Silence
chapters.summary: Ruth Ambrose is found dead, ruled a fall. Her will leaves Kestrel a key and a note: 'Count the anniversaries.' POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: grief hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Line
chapters.summary: Tracing the payments, Kestrel identifies the modern keeper: sexton Elias Marsh, whose family has served the crypt for six generations. He denies everything — badly. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: pity complicating suspicion.

chapters.title: Anniversary Night
chapters.summary: On the burial anniversary Kestrel stakes out the crypt and watches Elias carry food and a lantern inside. She follows him down. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: heart-pounding transgression.

chapters.title: Below the Cathedral
chapters.summary: In the sealed inner chamber Kestrel finds not a ghost but a living prisoner: Iris Vane, a young heir locked away by her family to keep the secret — and the inheritance — intact. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: horror and fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: Two Prisoners
chapters.summary: Iris tells her story: her father built the arrangement, Elias kept it out of inherited duty and fear. Kestrel realizes exposing the crime may doom Iris legally and socially. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: the price of survival made flesh.

chapters.title: The Family Reckons
chapters.summary: The Vane heirs discover the breach; their lawyer offers Kestrel money and silence, then veiled threats against Iris. Elias confesses his family's complicity to Kestrel privately. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: corruption wearing a lawful face.

chapters.title: A Case She Can't Close
chapters.summary: Cornered — discredited at work, followed, with no legal route to free Iris — Kestrel confronts her own limits and decides justice must happen outside the law. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: dark night of the soul.

chapters.title: The Long Night Below
chapters.summary: Kestrel, Elias, and Iris plan the exposure during the bicentennial reburial ceremony, when the crypt will be opened before the whole town. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: terrified determination.

chapters.title: Reburial
chapters.summary: As dignitaries lower the symbolic coffin, Kestrel steps forward, reads the decoded ledger aloud, and leads the crowd down into the crypt to Iris. Chaos erupts. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: the climax — truth spoken in the lion's den.

chapters.title: Justice, Unscheduled
chapters.summary: The heirs are arrested; the bishop tries to contain the scandal by firing Kestrel. Elias turns state's evidence. Iris walks into daylight for the first time in three years. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: costly vindication.

chapters.title: What the Town Owes
chapters.summary: Months later: memorial for the Harrow Fen victims, restitution proceedings, and a town learning to live without its flattering myth. Kestrel archives the ledger one last time. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: mourning and repair.

chapters.title: The Open Door
chapters.summary: Unemployed but unregretful, Kestrel visits the crypt, now a public memorial, and leaves the unlocked door open behind her. A stranger arrives asking for help with an old case. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: quiet renewal — the archivist begins again.
